title: AI Told Me to Start This Business. So I Did.
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Chris says he bought lazybooks.com for $800 before doing the research, then directs viewers to the site to subscribe for launch notifications. The validation segment promotes his own planned product.

stated_problem.quote: If you've used QuickBooks, you probably have noticed that the connection with your bank accounts always break and you have to reconnect it. It's really annoying and I've actually dug into that problem and it's very fixable.
stated_problem.speaker: Chris Koerner

idea.name: Lazy Books
idea.one_liner: Planned AI enabled accounting software for businesses with 0 to 10 employees, offered at a proposed $19 monthly subscription.
idea.customer: Businesses with 0 to 10 employees, initially focused on the US market.
idea.offer: Simple bookkeeping and accounting software with reliable bank feeds, core features, and an AI interface for asking questions about business finances.
idea.revenue_model: Proposed $19 per month subscription; the product has not launched.

key_quotes.quote: Reliable, affordable cloud accounting with rocksolid bank feeds.
And if you haven't figured it out by now, I'm actually going to launch this business.

19 bucks a month. It's not going to do the stuff that people hate about QuickBooks and Zero. And it is going to do the stuff that people love about QuickBooks and Zero. And it's going to be AI enabled.
So, you can ask questions about your business, about your financials. I'm going to have a simple toggle button to change the language from accountant to human cuz I don't speak accountant.
It's going to be built for businesses with 0 to 10 employees.

claims.claim: The proposed subscription price is $19 per month.
claims.quote: I'm thinking $19 a month and more simple core features only.

claims.claim: He estimates about 35 million US businesses, including 30 million with no employees, in the market.
claims.quote: There are about 35 million businesses in the United States, and I think 30 of them, 30 million of them have no employees.

claims.claim: The planned target segment is businesses with 0 to 10 employees.
claims.quote: It's going to be built for businesses with 0 to 10 employees.

claims.claim: He says his landing page method costs about $2 per year.
claims.quote: It's so easy and it costs about $2 a year the way I do it.

claims.claim: His Carrd plan costs about $50 a year and covers up to 25 websites.
claims.quote: I use card cru.co for all of my landing pages because it's like 50 bucks a year for up to 25 different websites.

claims.claim: A report suggested the product could have thousands of frustrated users ready to switch if it delivers reliable bank feeds, human support, and honest pricing.
claims.quote: If you can build reliable bank feeds, provide human support, and maintain honest pricing, you'll have thousands of frustrated users ready to switch.

claims.claim: He cites 35 million people in America as needing this type of service.
claims.quote: There are 35 million people in America that need one of these businesses, one of these services.

claims.claim: A report projected meaningful market share within two to three years with a 10x developer focused on the top three pain points.
claims.quote: With a 10x developer and a proper focus on the top three pain points, you can capture meaningful market share within two to three years.

claims.claim: He says he completed the landing page setup in eight minutes.
He paid $800 for the premium domain name.
claims.quote: So, I paid 800 bucks for this premium domain name.

acquisition_channels.details: He says he had already been asking his audience about QuickBooks and Xero, and directs video viewers to LazyBooks.com to subscribe for launch notifications.

ideas.delivery: The planned product is accounting software delivered online. The video demonstrates a landing page and email waitlist, but does not show the accounting product itself.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR and PECR apply to waitlist data and marketing emails; UK GDPR and security obligations apply to financial data. UK accounting customers would also make HMRC Making Tax Digital compatibility relevant.
